channel.title: Stanley Ngugi
channel.description: Technical writing by Stanley Ngugi on AI for formal methods, LLM theorem proving, grammar-constrained decoding, RL environments, and machine learning research.

item.title: An RL Environment Where C Code Has to Be Proved, Not Just Tested
item.description: An RL environment where models write C functions and reward comes from proving the code satisfies a fixed specification, rather than from passing a test suite.

item.title: How MathCheck RL Replaces Hidden Answer Keys with Lean-Checked Rewards
item.description: A math RL environment for bounded integer problems that replaces stored expected answers with full verification of each model submission against the encoded problem.

item.title: Building a Lean-Backed Verifier for Bounded Mathematical Answers
item.description: A verification engine that fully checks answers to bounded integer problems by generating executable Lean code over the entire finite domain, without requiring model-written proofs.

item.title: How a Grammar Changes AI-Generated Mathematical Proof Steps
item.description: A study of how grammar masking keeps language-model generations inside the shape of Lean tactics, preventing malformed proof steps without confusing valid syntax with proof correctness.

item.title: Building a Grammar for AI-Generated Mathematical Proof Steps
item.description: A practical study of Lean's tactic language: extracting tactic forms from real proofs, designing a grammar around them, and stress-testing what the grammar accepts and rejects.

item.title: Taming Incidental Polysemanticity in Toy Models: How Network Training Choices Affect Feature Entanglement
item.description: A toy-model investigation of whether feature entanglement is shaped during model training, with a ten-seed configuration comparison measured using sparse autoencoders.
